args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
[COUNTERPARTY MARKUP vs. FIRM-STANDARD POSITION]

---

ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This Account Control Agreement (this "Agreement") is made and entered as of [DATE] by and among [BORROWER] (the "Borrower"), [COLLATERAL AGENT] (the "Collateral Agent"), and [DEPOSITORY BANK] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Borrower maintains one or more deposit accounts (each an "Account" and, collectively, the "Accounts") with the Bank, as more particularly described on the signature pages and Exhibit A hereto;

WHEREAS, the Collateral Agent holds a security interest in the Accounts and all funds, securities and other property from time to time held therein, pursuant to that certain [EXECUTED CREDIT AGREEMENT]; and

WHEREAS, the parties desire to enter into this Agreement to perfect and protect the Collateral Agent's security interest in the Accounts in accordance with Section 9-104 of the Uniform Commercial Code.

NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:

**1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION**

1.1 As used herein, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

(a) "Account" means each deposit account listed on Exhibit A, as the same may be amended from time to time in accordance with Section 7.2.

(b) "Control" has the meaning set forth in Section 9-104 of the UCC.

(c) "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (i) the business, operations, properties, assets or financial condition of the Borrower, taken as a whole, or (ii) the ability of the Borrower to perform its obligations under this Agreement or any other Loan Document. **[COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: STRIKES existing definition and inserts:]** ~~Material Adverse Effect means a material adverse effect on the business, operations, properties, assets or financial condition of the Borrower, taken as a whole, or the ability of the Borrower to perform its obligations hereunder, except to the extent resulting from or arising out of (i) changes in general economic, financial or political conditions, (ii) changes in applicable laws, rules or regulations or the interpretation thereof by any governmental authority (including any regulatory action taken with respect to the Borrower), or (iii) any action taken or omitted to be taken by the Borrower at the written request or with the written consent of the Collateral Agent~~ **[REDLINE NOTE: Reject counterparty's addition of carve-outs (ii) and (iii). Firm-standard position requires no regulatory action carve-out. This carve-out directly intersects two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. See issues/risk memo Item 2.]**

(d) "Permitted Liens" means [firm-standard definition].

(e) "UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of [STATE].

**2. CONTROL OF ACCOUNTS**

2.1 The Bank shall comply with instructions originated by the Collateral Agent directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts (each, an "Entitlement Instruction") without further consent by the Borrower.

2.2 The Bank acknowledges that the Collateral Agent has Control over the Accounts for purposes of Section 9-104 of the UCC.

2.3 The Collateral Agent shall have the sole right to direct the disposition of funds in the Accounts, including the right to withdraw or transfer funds, subject to the terms of the [EXECUTED CREDIT AGREEMENT].

**3. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES**

3.1 The Borrower represents and warrants to the Collateral Agent and the Bank as of the date hereof and as of each date on which an Entitlement Instruction is delivered, that:

(a) it is validly existing and in good standing under the laws of [STATE];

(b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;

(c) this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms;

(d) it has not entered into any existing agreement with any person that conflicts with the Collateral Agent's Control over the Accounts;

(e) each Account is a "deposit account" within the meaning of the UCC and no third party (other than the Collateral Agent) has Control over any Account except as provided herein.

3.2 The Bank represents and warrants to the Borrower and the Collateral Agent as of the date hereof that:

(a) it is duly organized and validly existing under the laws of [STATE];

(b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;

(c) the Accounts listed on Exhibit A are maintained by the Bank in the ordinary course of its business.

3.3 **[SCHEDULE 3.7 DISCLOSURE]** The Borrower hereby discloses, as an exception to the representations set forth in Section 3.1, the matters set forth on Schedule 3.7. Such Schedule discloses two pending regulatory inquiries into the Borrower's banking operations and deposit account practices. **[REDLINE NOTE: The counterparty's proposed MAE carve-out for "regulatory action" at Section 1.1(c) is designed to and would operate to shield the Borrower from liability arising from these very inquiries, which are disclosed on Schedule 3.7. Reject the carve-out as drafted to ensure the representation in Section 3.1 and the MAE definition are not nullified by scheduled or unscheduled regulatory developments. See issues/risk memo Item 2.]**

**4. COVENANTS**

4.1 The Borrower shall not, without the prior written consent of the Collateral Agent:

(a) close, or permit the closing of, any Account;

(b) change the account number or other identifying information of any Account;

(c) enter into any agreement with any third party that would grant such third party Control over any Account; or

(d) take any other action that would result in the Collateral Agent no longer having Control over any Account.

**5. INDEMNIFICATION**

5.1 The Borrower agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Collateral Agent, its officers, directors, employees, agents and affiliates, from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred or suffered by the Collateral Agent arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Accounts, or the exercise by the Collateral Agent of its rights and remedies hereunder.

**[COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: Indemnification cap changed as follows:]**

~~5.2 The indemnification obligations of the Borrower under this Agreement shall be capped at an amount equal to [ORIGINAL: 100% of the total amounts held in the Accounts at the time of the triggering event]~~ **[REDLINE NOTE: Counterparty has silently reduced the cap. Firm-standard position is [BASE CAP]. See issues/risk memo Item 1.]**

~~5.3 The Borrower's indemnification obligations shall be subject to a deductible basket of [ORIGINAL BASKET AMOUNT], such basket operating as a threshold that must be exceeded before any indemnification payment is due.~~ **[COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: Converts deductible to tipping basket:]** *The Borrower's indemnification obligations shall be subject to a basket of [REDUCED THRESHOLD], such basket operating as a tipping basket, meaning that once the aggregate amount of indemnifiable losses exceeds the basket, the Borrower shall be obligated to indemnify the Collateral Agent for the full amount of all such losses (including amounts below the basket).* **[REDLINE NOTE: Per controlling deal team instruction (Doc. 110), client CONCEDES the basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket. Accept as modified. See issues/risk memo Item 1.]**

5.4 **[SCHEDULE 5.2 RETAINED LIABILITIES]** Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to expand the Borrower's indemnification obligations to cover the retained liabilities set forth on Schedule 5.2. The counterparty's proposed changes to Sections 5.2 and 5.3 would, if accepted in their entirety, silently shift a portion of these retained liabilities to the Collateral Agent through the reduced cap and converted basket. The firm-standard position preserves the Schedule 5.2 allocation. See issues/risk memo Item 1.]

**6. SURVIVAL**

6.1 All representations, warranties, covenants and indemnification obligations set forth in this Agreement shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement and the termination of the Accounts.

**[COUNTERPARTY MARKUP: Shortens survival period:]**

~~6.2 The representations and warranties set forth in Section 3 shall survive for [ORIGINAL: a period of [X] years] following the date of this Agreement.~~ **[Counterparty proposes:]** *The representations and warranties set forth in Section 3 shall survive for a period of [REDUCED: one (1) year] following the date of this Agreement.* **[REDLINE NOTE: REJECT — This contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B and constitutes a material reduction of core protection. Per controlling deal team instruction, any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. See issues/risk memo Item 3.]**

6.3 Exhibit B sets forth the agreed survival matrix for each representation, warranty, covenant and indemnification obligation. The survival periods set forth on Exhibit B are controlling and may not be amended except by a written instrument duly executed by all parties. **[REDLINE NOTE: Counterparty's proposed limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B. Restore firm-standard survival periods per Exhibit B. See issues/risk memo Item 3.]**

**7. MISCELLANEOUS**

7.1 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof.

7.2 The Accounts may be amended by written agreement among the parties, executed by all three parties hereto.

7.3 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of [STATE], without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.

7.4 Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in [COURT].

[Signature pages follow.]

---

**REDLINE SUMMARY — ALL TRACKED CHANGES:**

1. **§1.1(c) Material Adverse Effect Definition:** STRUCK the firm-standard carve-out-free definition; INSERTED counterparty's carve-out language for regulatory action, economic conditions, and consented actions. FIRM POSITION: REJECT insertions, restore firm-standard definition without regulatory carve-outs.

2. **§5.2 Indemnification Cap:** STRUCK original cap of [ORIGINAL CAP]; INSERTED reduced cap of [REDUCED CAP]. FIRM POSITION: REJECT reduction, restore original cap.

3. **§5.3 Indemnification Basket:** STRUCK deductible basket of [ORIGINAL BASKET]; INSERTED tipping basket of [REDUCED THRESHOLD]. FIRM POSITION: ACCEPT basket conversion per controlling deal instruction (client concedes conversion).

4. **§6.2 Survival Period:** STRUCK original [X]-year survival for core representations; INSERTED one-year survival. FIRM POSITION: REJECT — walk-away issue per controlling deal instruction.

5. **§6.3 Survival Matrix:** INSERTED confirmation that Exhibit B survival matrix is controlling, to prevent the counterparty's limitation period from overriding scheduled survival periods.

args.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Engagement File — Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
FROM: Contracts Group
DATE: [CURRENT DATE]
RE: Issues and Risk Memorandum — Counterparty Markup of Account Control Agreement

---

**I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

We have reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement against our internal playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, the account details, the disclosure schedules (including Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2), Exhibit B (survival matrix), and the controlling deal team correspondence. The counterparty's markup introduces four material deviations from firm-standard positions. Three of the four deviations must be rejected (indemnification cap reduction, MAE carve-outs, and survival-period reduction), and one is conceded by the client (basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket) pursuant to the controlling partner instruction.

Per the controlling correspondence (Doc. 110), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The deliverable reflects that priority ordering.

---

**II. DETAILED DEVIATION AND RISK ANALYSIS**

---

**ITEM 1: Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion**

**Section References:** §5.2, §5.3
**Approach in Counterparty Markup:** §5.2 silently reduces the indemnification cap; §5.3 converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket and reduces the threshold.
**Playbook/Firm-Standard Position:** The firm-standard form ("Firm ACA Playbook") provides for an indemnification cap equal to [100% of Account balances], with a deductible basket of [BASE AMOUNT]. The standard form does not permit a reduction in the cap and uses a deductible (not tipping) basket structure.

**Risk Rating: HIGH (cap reduction) / MODERATE (basket conversion)**

**Exposure Analysis:**
- **Cap reduction:** If the counterparty's reduced cap is accepted, the Collateral Agent's recovery could be limited to materially less than the value of the Accounts at the time a claim arises. In a scenario where the Accounts hold [ACCOUNT VALUE] at the time of an indemnifiable event, the reduced cap would cap recoveries at [REDUCED CAP], representing a loss of [DIFFERENCE] to the secured party. This dilution materially undermines the protections afforded by a control agreement, which is designed to give the Collateral Agent first-priority access to funds.
- **Basket conversion:** A tipping basket is actually more favorable to the indemnitee than a deductible basket, because once the basket is exceeded, the indemnitor must pay for all losses from the first dollar. However, the counterparty also reduced the basket threshold in the same clause, which narrows the scope of the protection. On a net basis, the conversion of the basket to a tipping structure is beneficial, but the threshold reduction must be analyzed carefully.

**Interaction with Schedule 5.2:** As disclosed on Schedule 5.2, the Borrower has certain retained liabilities that the parties agreed would not shift to the Collateral Agent. The combination of the reduced cap and the basket conversion in the counterparty's markup would, if fully accepted, silently shift the risk of losses from these retained liabilities onto the Collateral Agent, because indemnification recoveries against the Borrower would be capped at a reduced level while the liability exposure would be unchanged. Schedule 5.2 controls over general statements in the base materials, so any indemnification changes must be reconciled with that schedule.

**Required Reconciliation with Schedule 5.2:** The schedules explicitly state that scheduled exceptions narrow the representations and that the deliverable must reconcile both sources against the base materials. Accordingly, the accepted basket conversion must be expressly qualified so as not to shift Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.

**Recommended Position:**
- **Cap (§5.2):** REJECT the reduction. Maintain the firm-standard cap of [100% of Account balances]. Do not concede any reduction in the cap.
- **Basket (§5.3):** ACCEPT the conversion from deductible to tipping basket, per the controlling partner instruction. However, require that (i) the basket threshold be maintained at the firm-standard level (rather than the counterparty's reduced threshold), and (ii) the indemnification provisions operate subject to the allocation set forth on Schedule 5.2.

---

**ITEM 2: Material Adverse Effect Definition — Regulatory Action Carve-Out**

**Section References:** §1.1(c)
**Approach in Counterparty Markup:** Adds carve-outs from the definition of Material Adverse Effect for (i) general economic/financial/political conditions, (ii) changes in laws/rules/regulations or regulatory action taken with respect to the Borrower, and (iii) actions taken at the Collateral Agent's request or with its consent.
**Playbook/Firm-Standard Position:** The Firm ACA Playbook uses a MAE definition that (a) excludes general market/economic conditions, and (b) excludes actions taken at the secured party's request or with its consent. The playbook does NOT include a carve-out for regulatory action taken with respect to the Borrower, because that carve-out would undermine the fundamental risk allocation of a secured lending transaction where regulatory inquiries or enforcement are exactly the type of event that should constitute a MAE for lending purposes.

**Risk Rating: CRITICAL**

**Exposure Analysis:**
Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries into the Borrower's banking operations and deposit account practices. These inquiries directly intersect the proposed MAE carve-out. If the carve-out is accepted, the Borrower could argue that any adverse development arising from these regulatory inquiries does not constitute a MAE, thereby preventing the Collateral Agent from exercising remedies (including issuing entitlement instructions to direct funds) in response to regulatory-driven deterioration.

The exposure is not merely theoretical: the pending inquiries are already disclosed, and the carve-out is clearly drafted to shield the Borrower from consequences of these very inquiries. In a deposit-control context, where Control permits the Collateral Agent to direct the disposition of funds, a regulatory event that threatens the Accounts' value or availability directly impacts the collateral position. A MAE carve-out for regulatory action would effectively immunize the Borrower from the consequences of its own regulatory non-compliance, which is precisely the type of risk the MAE concept is intended to address.

**Regulatory Framework:** Under UCC §9-104, Control over a deposit account is essential to perfected secured status. If a regulatory action materially affected the Accounts (e.g., freeze, suspension, or regulatory downgrade), the Collateral Agent must be able to rely on the Accounts as collateral and exercise its entitlement instructions. The carve-out would undermine this protection.

**Recommended Position:**
- REJECT the counterparty's proposed carve-out for regulatory action. Restore the firm-standard MAE definition.
- If the counterparty insists on a regulatory carve-out, propose alternative language that excludes only "regulatory actions applicable to the banking or financial services industry generally and not the Borrower specifically," which maintains the playbook's intent while addressing the counterparty's legitimate concern about general regulatory risk. This is a fallback position and should not be offered unless necessary.
- Do not concede the carve-out with respect to the specific inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

---

**ITEM 3: Survival-Period Reduction for Core Representations**

**Section References:** §6.2, §6.3, Exhibit B
**Approach in Counterparty Markup:** Shortens the survival period for the core representations and warranties (Section 3) from the firm-standard [X] years to one (1) year.
**Playbook/Firm-Standard Position:** Exhibit B to the Firm ACA Playbook sets forth a survival matrix for each category of representations, warranties, covenants, and indemnification obligations. For core representations (including representations regarding borrowings, Liens, and Control), the playbook requires survival for the full [X]-year period. The counterparty's proposed one-year limitation contradicts Exhibit B.

**Risk Rating: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY**

**Exposure Analysis:**
A one-year survival period for core representations would leave the Collateral Agent without recourse for misrepresentations discovered after the survival period expires. In a secured transaction context, where collateral monitoring is ongoing, the Collateral Agent must maintain the ability to hold the Borrower accountable for misrepresentations throughout the life of the credit facility. A one-year survival window would be demonstrably insufficient to protect against post-closing discovery of misrepresentations, particularly given that the Borrower has already disclosed pending regulatory inquiries (Schedule 3.7) and retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) that may evolve over time.

**Controlling Instruction:** The latest controlling deal correspondence (Doc. 110) states that the client treats any survival-period reduction as a **walk-away issue**. Earlier messages in the thread stated a different priority ordering; only the latest message controls. Therefore, the survival-period reduction is a non-negotiable, walk-away condition.

**Interaction with Exhibit B:** Exhibit B sets forth the survival matrix that the counterparty's limitation-period change directly contradicts. The schedules and exhibits explicitly control over general statements in the base materials. Therefore, the survival periods on Exhibit B are binding and the counterparty's proposal to shorten them is a direct violation of the agreed document hierarchy.

**Recommended Position:**
- REJECT the survival-period reduction in its entirety. Maintain the survival periods set forth on Exhibit B.
- This is a **walk-away issue** per the controlling deal team instruction. If the counterparty does not withdraw its proposed limitation-period change, the transaction should not proceed.
- Add express confirmation in §6.3 that Exhibit B's survival matrix is controlling and may not be amended except by written agreement of all parties.
- If the counterparty persists, recommend that the deal team be advised that the matter cannot proceed without withdrawal of this deviation.

---

**ITEM 4: Missing Protections**

In addition to the deviations introduced by the counterparty markup, the review identified certain protections that must be present in a market-standard Account Control Agreement but were omitted from the draft:

**(a) No-Action Language for Borrower Instructions.** The draft should include an express provision that the Bank may not act on Borrower instructions that are inconsistent with the Collateral Agent's Entitlement Instructions, and that any conflict shall be resolved in favor of the Collateral Agent. This is a firm-standard provision required by the playbook.

**(b) Set-Off Acknowledgment.** The draft should contain an acknowledgment that the Bank does not have a right of set-off against the Accounts, or if it does, an express subordination of that right to the Collateral Agent's interest.

**(c) Notice Provisions for Bank.** The draft should include a provision obligating the Bank to provide the Collateral Agent with prompt notice of any adverse claim, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process affecting the Accounts.

**Risk Rating: MODERATE**
**Exposure Analysis:** These missing provisions are standard in depository control agreements and are required for the Collateral Agent to have full confidence in its Control position. While their absence does not, by itself, invalidate Control under UCC §9-104, it creates practical and operational gaps that could impede the Collateral Agent's ability to exercise Control in a fast-moving situation.

**Recommended Position:** Insert the missing protections in the redline per the firm-standard playbook language.

---

**III. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX**

| # | Section | Term | Counterparty Change | Firm-Standard Position | Risk Rating | Disposition |
|---|---------|------|---------------------|------------------------|-------------|-------------|
| 1 | §5.2 | Indemnification Cap | Reduced cap | Cap = [100% of Account balances] | HIGH | REJECT |
| 2 | §5.3 | Indemnification Basket | Deductible→tipping basket; reduced threshold | Deductible basket at [BASE] | MODERATE | ACCEPT conversion (per controlling instruction); reject threshold reduction |
| 3 | §1.1(c) | MAE Definition | Adds regulatory action carve-out | No regulatory carve-out | CRITICAL | REJECT |
| 4 | §6.2 | Survival Period | Reduced to 1 year | [X]-year survival per Exhibit B | CRITICAL | REJECT — Walk-away |
| 5 | Various | Missing protections (no-action, set-off, bank notices) | Omitted from draft | Required by playbook | MODERATE | INSERT in redline |

---

**IV. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS**

Three of the four counterparty deviations must be rejected: the indemnification cap reduction (§5.2), the MAE regulatory carve-outs (§1.1(c)), and the survival-period reduction (§6.2). Of these, the survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue per the controlling partner instruction. The basket conversion (§5.3) may be accepted as conceded by the client, subject to maintaining the firm-standard basket threshold and reconciling with Schedule 5.2.

We recommend: (i) return the redline to the counterparty with the tracked-changes positions set forth herein; (ii) flag the survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue to the deal team; and (iii) if the counterparty persists on the survival-period reduction, escalate to the engagement partner for go/no-go decision.
